On a large-scale zebrafish EM segmentation they run distributed skeletonization on Google Cloud, cluster neurons with NBLAST, and jointly examine morphological similarity and connectivity. They position the stack, with BigArrays.jl, for terabyte-scale volumes. Code and notebooks are on GitHub (seung-lab / jingpengw).
summaries.advanced: This is a software methods paper; “suitable for terabyte-scale” is a demonstration claim, not a timed bake-off in the extract. Catalog authors list Ting Zhao, who appears as handling editor, not a paper author. Catalog datasets tag zebrafish, matching the demonstration volume. NBLAST clustering quality is illustrated, not scored against a public morphology gold standard here. Sparse skeletonization assumes a segmentation already exists.

plain_language_summary: Computers that color in neurons still leave a blob, not a stick-figure skeleton. This Julia toolbox turns huge electron-microscope segmentations into skeletons you can measure and compare, shown on a zebrafish dataset in the cloud.

ocar.opportunity: Feeding initiation must combine taste quality with hunger; adult Drosophila genetics plus EM can expose a sensorimotor path from gustatory neurons to proboscis motor neurons.
ocar.challenge: Prior work knew sensory neurons, motor neurons, and a few interneurons, not a complete local circuit or where hunger and bitter conflict act.
ocar.action: Shiu, Sterne, Engert, Dickson, and Scott, in eLife (2022), reconstruct a gustatory sensorimotor circuit at synaptic resolution and combine it with targeted physiology and behavior for adult Drosophila feeding initiation.
ocar.resolution: The pathway links gustatory sensory neurons to proboscis motor neurons through three intermediate layers; most neurons are necessary and/or sufficient for extension and respond selectively to sugar. Hunger amplifies at select second-order neurons; a bitter pathway inhibits at premotor neurons, implementing a local sugar-versus-bitter weighing. Single-cell inhibition never abolished extension, matching multiple parallel routes to MN9.
ocar.future_work: How water taste gates extension in thirsty flies is left open; they note no direct GRN–motor synapses for this adult program, unlike some larval feeding paths.

summaries.beginner: A fly starts eating only if food tastes good and the animal is hungry. This paper maps a short brain circuit from taste sensors to the muscles of the feeding snout, and shows hunger boosting an early step while bitter brakes a later step.
summaries.intermediate: In eLife (2022), Shiu, Sterne, and colleagues reconstruct an adult Drosophila feeding-initiation circuit from gustatory receptor neurons to proboscis motor neurons with three intermediate layers. Most neurons in the path elicit proboscis extension when activated and respond to sugar rather than water or bitter in food-deprived flies. Hunger signals amplify at select second-order neurons; bitter inhibition impinges on premotor neurons. Inhibiting single second-order cells reduced extension, whereas inhibiting individual third-order or premotor cells did not, consistent with multiple routes from sugar GRNs to MN9.
summaries.advanced: Catalog journal field lists bioRxiv; the PDF is the eLife article (DOI 10.7554/eLife.79887). “Complete” refers to this reconstructed sugar-to-MN9 path, not all feeding subprograms (e.g., pumping). Necessity is incomplete at the single-cell level by the authors’ own results. Water/thirst gating is explicitly unsolved. Parallel paths are inferred from connectivity plus incomplete silencing, not from a full lesion set of every route.

plain_language_summary: A fly starts eating only if food tastes good and the animal is hungry. This paper maps a short brain circuit from taste sensors to the muscles of the feeding snout, and shows hunger boosting an early step while bitter brakes a later step.

ocar.opportunity: Accurate directed, weighted brainstem connectivity is needed to model lesions and signal flow in disease, using rat tract-tracing as a gold-standard substrate.
ocar.challenge: Overlapping nomenclatures and repeated reports of the same projection create variability unless every observation is preserved rather than collapsed.
ocar.action: Schmitt, Eipert, Ruß, Beier, Kadir, and Horn, in Scientific Data (2022), release the brainstem connectome (BC) database of all known directed, weighted connections of adult rat brainstem nuclei, collated from original tract-tracing papers into neuroVIISAS with web and table access.
ocar.resolution: Graph analyses describe BC as scale-free with small-world connectivity; Louvain modularity and weighted stochastic block matching partly aligned communities with function. FitzHugh–Nagumo simulations of a somatosensory path showed that linearly decreasing weights (a demyelination-like manipulation) reduced primary somatosensory cortex potentials more than some earlier stations (Cu, VPL).
ocar.future_work: They note that multiple inputs/outputs along the path will interfere, so further work is needed to interpret distant dynamical effects of a local weight change; JAVA/neuroVIISAS code is provided.

summaries.beginner: The brainstem is a crowded junction of vital pathways, but its directed wiring has been scattered across decades of tracing papers. This database gathers those rat connections so researchers can measure the network and simulate what happens when links weaken, as in multiple sclerosis.
summaries.intermediate: In Scientific Data (2022), Schmitt and colleagues publish a meta-analytic rat brainstem connectome that keeps duplicate observations of the same projection. The resource is queryable via tables, a web tool, and neuroVIISAS. Analyses report scale-free, small-world organization and communities that partly match function (Louvain and weighted SBM). An example FitzHugh–Nagumo simulation of DRG → brainstem → contralateral VPL → S1 shows stable oscillations; a linear weight decrease on the first-order somatosensory connections, intended to mimic demyelination, relatively suppressed S1_r membrane potentials compared with Cu_l and VPL_r.
summaries.advanced: This is tract-tracing meta-data, not synapse-resolution EM. “All known connections” means collated published TT reports, with nomenclature-translation caveats the authors themselves mention. Scale-free/small-world are graph summaries of the collated directed weighted network. FHN demyelination is a selective weight change in a model, not a clinical MS reconstruction. Catalog tags include proofreading; the paper is a database/metastudy, not EM proofreading.

plain_language_summary: The brainstem is a crowded junction of vital pathways, but its directed wiring has been scattered across decades of tracing papers. This database gathers those rat connections so researchers can measure the network and simulate what happens when links weaken, as in multiple sclerosis.
